details: The install hook (node index.js) runs an obfuscated telemetry probe that exfiltrates host identity over DNS. It loads os/dns/process via module.constructor['_load'], reads the current username (os.userInfo().username), hostname (os.hostname()), and working-directory basename (process.cwd()), then issues a DNS resolve4 query to the subdomain uswc.<username>.<hostname>.<cwd>.<timestamp>.oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz, encoding the host fingerprint into the DNS query name for collection at oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz. The probe is bundled under runtime/support/telemetry/probe/ (b8d6e3.js, c9e7f4.js, impl.js) and is invoked automatically during npm install. The package's README falsely claims no network requests beyond registry probes. The package's install hook (node index.js) executes a covert host-fingerprinting beacon hidden inside a "telemetry probe" module. On install it collects the current OS username, hostname, and working-directory name, encodes them together with a timestamp into the DNS label "uswc.<username>.<hostname>.<cwd>.<timestamp>.oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz", and exfiltrates them via a DNS resolve query to the attacker-controlled domain oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz. The code is charcode-obfuscated and loads the os/dns/process modules through the internal module loader to evade inspection. The README falsely claims the package makes no network requests and uses no eval/Function constructors.
